Interventions on binary exposures

natural.Rd

Constructors of the interventions compared by intervene_effect().

Usage

natural()

setto(values)

shift(delta, from = 1, to = 0)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_intervention'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

values

Integer 0/1 vector: values for the intervened exposures.

delta

Probability (between 0 and 1) of moving an exposure from from to to.

from, to

Exposure values (0 or 1, different).

x

An lcc_intervention object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class lcc_intervention: a list with type ("natural", "set" or "shift"), values, delta, from, to and a label used in output. The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

  • natural(): the natural course (no intervention); the usual comparison g0.

  • setto(values): static intervention setting the intervened exposures to values (one 0/1 value per intervened exposure, in the order they were selected), for everyone.

  • shift(delta, from = 1, to = 0): stochastic intervention that depends on the natural value of the exposure (a modified treatment policy; Haneuse & Rotnitzky 2013; Díaz et al. 2023): each intervened exposure that equals from is moved to to with probability delta, independently. shift(1) removes the exposure entirely, shift(0.5) halves its prevalence.

References

Haneuse, S., & Rotnitzky, A. (2013). Estimation of the effect of interventions that modify the received treatment. Statistics in Medicine, 32(30), 5260–5277. doi:10.1002/sim.5907

Díaz, I., Williams, N., Hoffman, K. L., & Schenck, E. J. (2023). Nonparametric causal effects based on longitudinal modified treatment policies. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 118(542), 846–857. doi:10.1080/01621459.2021.1955691

See also

intervene_effect()

Examples

natural()
#> <intervention> natural course
setto(c(0, 0))
#> <intervention> set to (0, 0)
shift(0.5)
#> <intervention> shift 1→0 with probability 0.5
shift(0.2, from = 0, to = 1)
#> <intervention> shift 0→1 with probability 0.2
